About Team:
Our team collaborates with Walmart International, which has over 5,900 retail units operating outside of the United States under 55 banners in 26 countries including Africa, Argentina, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India, Japan, and Mexico, to name a few.
What Youll Do
  • Design and build highly scalable, resilient backend services for Order Management Systems (OMS) and Fulfillment Management Systems (FMS) serving multiple international markets (MX, CA, and beyond).
  • Architect and implement multi-tenant / multi-market solutions that support locale-specific business rules, tax regulations, fulfillment models, and delivery SLAs across geographies.

  • Partner with Data Engineering and Data Science teams to enable AI/ML-driven capabilities such as intelligent order routing, demand forecasting integration, and anomaly detection in fulfillment pipelines.

  • Strong experience with NoSQL databases (Cassandra, Cosmos DB, MongoDB, or similar) and understanding of data modeling trade-offs for high-scale systems.

  • Experience supporting multi-market / multi-tenant platforms with locale-aware business logic, internationalization (i18n), and cross-border considerations.
  • Strong understanding of cloud-native development on Azure or GCP - managed services, infrastructure as code (Terraform), CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience with AI/ML literacy and applications - understanding of how machine learning models are integrated into production systems, leveraging GenAI/LLM tools for developer productivity (e.g., code generation, automated testing, intelligent debugging), and staying current with AI-driven engineering practices.

  • Experience with feature flagging, A/B testing, and progressive rollout strategies for multi-market deployments.
  • Proficiency in system design, domain-driven design (DDD), and API design (REST, gRPC, GraphQL).
  • Track record of leading technical initiatives, driving architecture decisions, and influencing without authority across teams.
Nice to Have
  • Prior experience in Order Management, Fulfillment, Supply Chain, or eCommerce domain systems.
  • Familiarity with OMS platforms (Sterling, custom-built) and fulfillment orchestration patterns.
  • Contributions to open-source projects or technical community leadership.

jobDescription:
About Marvell
Marvell s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.
Your Team, Your Impact
As a Principal Engineer-DFT with Marvell, you ll be a member of the Connectivity business group. Connectivity solutions from Marvell help customers address the growing demands of AI, cloud computing, edge computing, 5G networks, and next-generation data centers. Engineers within the Connectivity Business Unit work on cutting-edge silicon design, firmware, software, system validation, and platform development, collaborating across global teams to deliver products that connect billions of devices and accelerate digital transformation.

Joining the Connectivity Business Unit offers the opportunity to work on complex technical challenges, influence next-generation connectivity technologies, and contribute to products deployed at global scale.
What You Can Expect
  • Define and drive DFT architecture and implementation strategies for complex SoC/ASIC designs.
  • Develop and implement scan, compression, MBIST, and other DFT features to achieve test coverage and manufacturing quality goals.
  • Execute and support scan insertion, DFT verification, and ATPG flows.
  • Collaborate closely with RTL, verification, physical design, timing, and product engineering teams throughout the design lifecycle.
  • Create and maintain DFT-related timing constraints and signoff requirements.
  • Perform DFT timing analysis and debug timing-related issues.
  • Drive DFT methodology improvements and contribute to flow automation.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior engineers.
What Were Looking For

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Principal Engineer - Design for Test (DFT) to lead DFT architecture, implementation, and signoff activities for complex SoC and ASIC designs. The ideal candidate will have deep expertise in DFT methodologies, scan insertion, ATPG, timing constraints, and test architecture development, with a proven track record of delivering high-quality silicon products.

Required Qualifications
  • Bachelors or Masters degree in Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
  • 14+ years of experience in Design for Test (DFT) for ASIC/SoC development.
  • Strong expertise in DFT methodologies, including scan architecture, scan compression, ATPG, Memory BIST, Boundary Scan and testability concepts.
  • Hands-on experience with Siemens EDA Tessent tools.
  • Strong experience with synthesis and scan insertion tools.
  • Solid understanding and hands on experience of Static Timing Analysis (STA) and timing closure concepts.
  • Experience creating and managing SDC (Synopsys Design Constraints) files for DFT implementation and timing signoff.
  • Strong debugging, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn t a buzzword - it s a way of life. Who We Are and Where Were Going
Assurance at Salesforce is being rebuilt as an engineering discipline.
Legacy GRC runs on spreadsheets, screenshots, and an annual scramble to prove that controls worked months ago. Were replacing that model with one that is continuous, automated, and built into how Salesforce ships. Controls are code. Evidence comes from pipelines, not people chasing tickets. We work to improve the state of controls, drive decisions with risk, govern with code, and make compliance a streamlined business process.
Our strategy:
Risk-informed, control managed. We monitor, validate, and improve the security controls that stand against threats and failures. This proves trust while delivering risk operations, compliance artifacts, and outputs, and it opens access to new markets through the product we build and the behavior we change.
Visibility and invention. We give Salesforce a clear, current view of its security posture. We equip the Assurance team with a new way of protecting Salesforce, through the invention we create together. We also invest in the people who work here, with room to grow, take on new challenges, and drive excellence.
Always in front. We turn gaps into signals, alerts, and escalations. When a control fails, it flows into a workflow built to help stakeholders meet their trust obligations. Nothing waits for the next audit to surface.
Were hiring people who want to build this future. Youll have real ownership, a real roadmap, and the chance to define what modern assurance looks like for the industry.
What you ll do
Risk Operations provides a centralized approach to identifying, prioritizing, and managing cybersecurity risks, driving accountability, faster decision-making, and measurable risk reduction. The team partners across security, engineering, and business functions to streamline risk management processes, improve visibility into risk exposure, and ensure timely escalation and resolution.
Were looking for an Information Security Associate who is excited to help build and support a growing Risk Operations function. In this role, youll be at the center of day-to-day security issue and exception management activities, helping ensure risk cases are accurately documented, efficiently processed, and consistently tracked through resolution. Youll work closely with experienced risk and security professionals while contributing to the development of workflows, processes, and reporting that will help shape how Risk Operations operates at scale.
This is a great opportunity for an early-career security professional who enjoys solving problems, bringing organization to complex processes, and making a meaningful impact in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
  • Rapid Decision Management: We work in a business. Predictability and rapid decisions are the core outcomes you ll bring to the job. Support rapid risk decision-making by coordinating timely reviews, approvals, and escalations, ensuring decision-makers have the information needed to assess risks and take action.
  • Support day-to-day security risk operations by managing the intake, triage, and tracking of security issues and exceptions to accelerate risk-based decisions and timely resolution.
  • Coordinate issue and exception management activities, including reviewing submissions for completeness, following up with stakeholders, tracking remediation commitments, monitoring exception expiration dates, and supporting timely case resolution.
  • Maintain accurate and complete risk records in case management platforms, ensuring consistent documentation, appropriate case status, and reliable data for operational reporting.
  • Partner with security, engineering, and compliance teams to gather information, clarify case requirements, resolve operational blockers, and accelerate risk-based decision-making by ensuring stakeholders have the information, context, and visibility needed to take timely action.
  • Support timely risk decisions and escalations by monitoring case progress, identifying stalled requests or decision gaps, and coordinating follow-ups to ensure issues and exceptions move efficiently through established governance and approval workflows.
  • Assist with operational reporting and metrics, including tracking case volumes, aging, remediation progress, exception renewals, and other key performance indicators to provide visibility into risk operations activities.
  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency and automate repetitive tasks, helping streamline case handling, improve data quality, and enhance the overall stakeholder experience.
  • Contribute to broader Risk Operations initiatives by supporting ad hoc requests, process improvements, and emerging operational needs as the team establishes and matures its capabilities.
What you bring ...
  • You have +2 years of experience in information security or security operations, or a related field.
  • You have a foundational understanding of information security concepts, including security findings, risk remediation, policy exceptions, and risk acceptance.
  • You have sufficient technical ability to serve as one of many eyes as we assess the certainty of our compensating controls and exposures.
  • You are highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple cases, deadlines, and follow-up activities while maintaining accurate records.
  • You bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to review information for completeness, identify inconsistencies, and recognize when issues require additional attention or escalation.
  • You have strong written and verbal communication skills and enjoy collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to gather information, clarify requirements, and drive timely follow-through.
  • You are comfortable learning new tools, navigating workflow or ticketing systems, and working with spreadsheets and data to support operational activities.
  • You are adaptable, proactive, and comfortable working in an evolving environment where processes and responsibilities are still being established.
  • You have a continuous improvement mindset and are eager to learn, contribute ideas, and help build scalable and efficient security risk management practices.
How We Work
  • Engineering-first culture. We use version control, code review, CI/CD, and backlogs. Assurance work ships like software.
  • Automate first. If its done manually twice, its a candidate for a build.
  • Signals, not surprises. Gaps become alerts and workflows, and control failures resolve through defined escalation paths.
  • Embedded partners. We work alongside T&P teams and solve problems with them, not at them.
  • Outcomes over activity. We measure risk reduced, effort saved, and audit friction removed.
  • Room to grow. Learn the engineering side if you come from GRC, or the risk side if you come from engineering. We support both paths.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Intelligence
jobDescription:
About the role:

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Intelligence team, you will own a significant part of that stack end to end. Depending on your background and interest, that could be the machine learning training and serving path, the AI agent runtime, the data platform, the learned control policies running on our edge devices, or the backend services that connect them.


Ownership here means more than writing the code. It means understanding how your subsystem fails, deciding what should not be built, explaining the trade-offs to the people who will live with them, and being someone others come to when a number looks wrong.

You will also work close to the customer. Our users are facility teams, energy managers and plant operators, and the fastest way to understand why something is not working is to watch one of them try to use it. Engineers here shape what gets built, not only how it gets built.

We are a small team with a large surface area, so you will have unusual latitude and unusual responsibility for the parts you take on.



Our tech stack

  • Languages — Python (primary), JavaScript, TypeScript
  • Machine learning — scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras, pandas, numpy, AWS SageMaker
  • Reinforcement learning and control — RL policies, classical PID, lookup-based control, running on constrained edge hardware
  • AI systems — AWS Bedrock, agent loops, tool registries, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt caching, model tiering, grounding and verification, evaluation harnesses
  • Data platform — Apache Airflow, InfluxDB, Timestream, PostgreSQL, Redis, DynamoDB, S3
  • Knowledge graph — Amazon Neptune, Brick schema, RDF and SPARQL
  • Observability — Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Sentry, OpenTelemetry, CloudWatch
  • Backend and front end — FastAPI, Node.js with streaming interfaces, Angular
  • Edge — Python on ARM Linux, MQTT, local PostgreSQL, systemd
  • Cloud and infrastructure — AWS, Docker, GitHub Actions


What you will do:

  • Own the design, implementation and production behaviour of a subsystem, including its failure modes
  • Take machine learning models from experiment to production — training pipelines, deployment, monitoring, retraining, and an honest assessment of when a prediction should not be acted upon
  • Work on the learned control policies whose decisions become physical actions on real machinery
  • Build and improve our AI systems: retrieval and tool-calling agents grounded in a knowledge graph and live telemetry, with evaluation frameworks that measure whether the answers are actually right
  • Debug across the whole stack, from an edge device in a plant room through message transport, storage and APIs to what a user finally sees
  • Partner with product managers and customers to define what gets built, and offer a different view, with reasoning, when a requirement does not hold up
  • Present your work to technical and non-technical audiences alike, including customers
  • Review code, write design documents others can act on, and mentor engineers earlier in their careers


You may be a good fit if you have:

  • Around 4–5 years building and running production software, with strong Python and working depth in at least one of Node.js, a front-end framework, or an ML serving stack
  • Machine learning in production — models that real decisions depended on, and first-hand experience of drift, retraining, and the gap between an offline metric and live behaviour. Depth in classical ML, deep learning and neural networks, or both
  • Strong statistical foundations and the instinct to explore data before modelling it. Much of our work begins with messy sensor data, and knowing what a distribution, a correlation or an outlier is actually telling you decides whether the model that follows is worth anything
  • LLM systems in production — a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline, an agent with tool use, a structured extraction system, or something similar, that real users depended on. Built on AWS Bedrock, LangChain, or direct provider APIs. We are as interested in how you evaluated it and how you prevented confident wrong answers as in what you built
  • A working understanding of reinforcement learning — agents, states, actions, rewards, and why an RL policy behaves differently from a supervised model. We run RL in production, so hands-on depth is a strong advantage
  • Fluency with AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor as part of your daily work. A large share of first-draft code here is AI-assisted, so knowing how to review it, catch its errors and decide what to keep is a core skill
  • Worked with data infrastructure at some depth — time-series databases, caching or streaming systems — and formed opinions about staleness, consistency and back-pressure
  • Been responsible for something with real users and real downtime, and learned from it
  • Experience collaborating with product managers or customers to decide what to build, not only to receive specifications
  • Clear written communication. Design documents and post-mortems here are read widely


Nice to have:

  • Open source contributions — a library you maintain, sustained contributions to a project, or work that others build on
  • Reinforcement learning applied to a real physical system rather than a simulator alone
  • Deep learning applied to time-series, sequence or control problems
  • Experience with building automation, HVAC, or industrial control systems
  • Knowledge graphs, ontologies, or semantic data modelling
  • Running orchestration platforms such as Airflow at a scale where they became difficult
  • Embedded or edge deployment on constrained hardware
  • Having owned a product area rather than only a codebase

The Senior Specialist, Privacy and Technology Compliance supports privacy and technology compliance program through privacy impact assessments, data handling reviews, and technology compliance assessments. The role works with product, engineering, and business teams to identify privacy and technology risks early and recommend practical mitigations.


Assessments follow a template; the risks often do not. A feature uses data in a way nobody described as new, a vendors data flow crosses a border that was not in scope, or a technical control exists but does not do what the assessment assumes. The role is expected to ask the questions that surface these, and to be clear about the residual risk. These are the cases the role exists to get right.


Privacy Officer accountability, risk acceptance, and final approval decisions remain.

Privacy Operations Support:

  • 6-8 years in privacy, data protection, or technology compliance.
  • Degree in law, information systems, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

title: Project Lead - AI Strategy & Operating Models
jobDescription:
Role & responsibilities

Project Lead
Employment Type: Full-time

About Zinnov

Zinnov is a global management consulting firm that helps organizations make decisions that get used and deliver results that matter. For over two decades, we’ve partnered with leading enterprises, high-growth technology companies, and investors to answer some of the toughest questions they face:

Where should we invest?

How do we scale globally?

What capabilities will win in the next decade?

Our work shapes market entry strategies, global operating models, M&A decisions, and long-term growth bets. We’re known for being data-led, execution-focused, and outcome-driven — not opinion-heavy slideware.

At Zinnov, how you work matters as much as what you deliver. We value independent thinking, crisp communication, and early ownership. With 450+ professionals across 10 global offices, we work across industries including Digital Services, ER&D, Enterprise Software, Semiconductors, Healthcare, BFSI, Automotive, Media & Telecom, and Private Equity.

Zinnov isn’t for everyone. It’s for people who want steep learning curves, honest feedback, and the chance to see their work influence real business decisions — not just presentations.

Why Globalization Excellence (GE)

Zinnov’s Globalization Excellence (GE) practice helps enterprises build, scale and transform Global Capability Centers (GCCs) end-to-end — from Design & Discovery to Build, Scale, to transform.

In GE, you don’t work in silos. You:

Own complex, end-to-end client journeys

Work across GCC advisory, managed services, and advise on BOT / outsourcing models

Influence leadership decisions that shape long-term talent and operating strategies

This is where strategy meets execution — and where talent plays a defining role.

About the Role

Help global enterprises rethink how work gets done in an AI-driven world. You will support AI strategy, workforce planning and AI-native GCC engagements—assessing how GenAI, automation and AI agents change processes, roles, productivity and operating models, then turning insights into actionable business cases and transformation roadmaps. This is a management consulting role, not an AI engineering position.

In a few years here, you will see more decisions about where and how work gets done than most executives see in a career: what works, where things stall, and which mistakes get expensive. You will help clients determine which work AI can augment or automate, what people and capabilities they will need, and how AI-native GCCs should operate. The goal is not to agree with the initial brief; it is to identify the better decision and help make it real.

Our standard is to be the person a client calls before the decision is made. Ask: What is the real problem behind the request? What can we tell them that they do not already know? What should they not do?

What You’ll Do

A CXO may ask what AI can change in a 400-person support operation or whether a new GCC should be designed around 80 AI-enabled roles rather than 150 conventional ones. Your job is to answer the question—and find the more important question underneath it.

  • Frame the problem. Scope AI transformation and workforce challenges; interview stakeholders, test assumptions, and assess AI readiness, process suitability and business priorities.
  • Build the case. Assess task-level automation and augmentation potential; model workforce demand, role evolution, productivity, skills gaps, cost implications and AI use-case value, distinguishing evidence from estimates.
  • Make the call. Recommend AI adoption priorities, future-state human–AI operating models and AI-native GCC capabilities; articulate trade-offs, risks and what clients should avoid.
  • Run the work. Own consulting workstreams or smaller projects, managing analysis, client updates, milestones, risks and high-quality executive-ready outputs.
  • Follow through. Translate recommendations into workforce transition plans, reskilling priorities, governance and phased implementation roadmaps; track whether anticipated benefits materialize.
  • Build the practice. Contribute to proposals, reusable AI workforce models, research and perspectives on AI-led engineering productivity, future of work and GCC transformation.

Preferred candidate profile


What You’ll Bring

  • 3–8 years in management consulting, strategy, AI/digital transformation advisory, workforce or organization transformation, or related business strategy roles.
  • Practical understanding of GenAI, AI copilots, agentic AI and automation—and how they change workflows, roles, workforce capacity and enterprise operating models.
  • Strong structured problem-solving and quantitative skills: workforce scenarios, cost/productivity modelling, business cases and clear recommendations.
  • Experience owning deliverables or workstreams, engaging stakeholders and communicating credibly with senior decision-makers.
  • Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint; strong research, synthesis and executive storytelling skills.

Preferred: AI strategy or workforce planning engagements; organizational redesign; GCC or global operating model exposure

What Success Looks Like

At 6 months: Independently own an AI transformation or workforce analysis workstream; produce defensible productivity and workforce scenarios; deliver recommendations that influence a client decision with minimal rework.

At 12 months: Lead multiple workstreams or a smaller engagement; shape an AI workforce or AI-native GCC transformation roadmap adopted by a client; demonstrate evidence of business impact and contribute a reusable practice asset.

title: Lead Data / AI Architect
jobDescription:
We are looking for a Lead Data Architect to design, build, and scale our data pipelines and entity resolution systems. This role combines deep technical expertise in data engineering with hands-on experience in AI-assisted tooling, entity matching, and data integration from diverse sources. You will lead architectural decisions for our data platform, mentor engineers, and ensure our pipelines are reliable, scalable, and production-grade.

Key Responsibilities
  • Architect, build, and maintain robust, scalable data pipelines that ingest, transform, and serve data from multiple internal and external sources.
  • Own the end-to-end orchestration of data workflows using tools like Dagster, ensuring observability, reliability, and maintainability of pipelines.
  • Design and implement entity resolution workflows, including matching, merging, and survivorship logic, using tools such as Splink, to produce clean, deduplicated, golden records.
  • Build and maintain web scrapers to source data from external providers, ensuring resilience to source changes, rate limits, and data quality issues.
  • Integrate and reconcile data coming from multiple, often inconsistent, sources into unified, trustworthy datasets.
  • Design and maintain data models and schemas across transactional and analytical systems, ensuring consistency, scalability, and performance.
  • Leverage AI/LLM-based tools and techniques to enhance data pipeline capabilities, e.g., intelligent data extraction, automated data quality checks, or AI-assisted entity matching.
  • Define and enforce best practices around pipeline design, testing, monitoring, and documentation.
  • Collaborate closely with data engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders to translate business requirements into scalable data architecture.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to the data engineering team.
Required Skills & Experience
  • Strong hands-on experience building and maintaining production-grade data pipelines at scale.
  • Practical experience with Dagster (or similar orchestration tools like Airflow/Prefect) for pipeline orchestration.
  • Experience with Splink or similar probabilistic/deterministic record linkage tools for entity matching, merging, and survivorship.
  • Strong proficiency in Python, including experience writing and maintaining web scrapers.
  • Proven experience integrating and maintaining data pipelines that pull from multiple, heterogeneous data sources.
  • Experience applying AI/ML tools within data engineering workflows (e.g., LLM-assisted data cleaning, extraction, or matching).
  • Hands-on experience with relational and distributed databases such as PostgreSQL and Google Cloud Spanner.
  • Strong understanding of data modeling principles (normalization, dimensional modeling, schema design) across OLTP and OLAP systems.
  • Experience with cloud data warehousing platforms such as BigQuery, Redshift, and cloud platforms (GCP/AWS/Azure).
  • Strong communication skills and experience working cross-functionally with engineering and product teams.

  • Familiarity with data governance, lineage, and cataloging tools.
  • Prior experience in a lead or architect-level role guiding a data engineering team.

Position Overview:As a Platform Hardware Design Engineer, you will contribute to the end-to-end development of advanced platform hardware, translating platform level requirements into circuit and component level specifications and ultimately into high quality board designs.You will work across the hardware development lifecycle, including architecture and requirements definition, component selection, schematic design, PCB implementation, design reviews, board fabrication and assembly support, power-on, bring-up, debug, validation, and delivery.This is a hands-on engineering role for candidates who enjoy solving complex hardware problems and working across disciplines to turn system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware.Our Business GroupYou will be joining the Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE), an organization at Intel committed to advancing Intel's mission of delivering world class silicon and platform solutions. The group focuses on developing integrated systems that align with customer needs and support Intel's broader goals of leadership in technology innovation. SPE collaborates across diverse domains to ensure Intel platforms meet performance, reliability, and scalability requirements.Our work sits at the intersection of silicon, board hardware, firmware, validation, signal and power integrity, mechanical and thermal engineering, PCB technology, manufacturing, and system integration.Our hardware engineers have a broader responsibility than executing an individual design. They help establish platform architecture, guide implementation, identify and qualify appropriate hardware solutions, provide technical leadership during board power-on and debug, and lead resolution of schematic, layout, SI/PI, and hardware issues. title: AI Developer Intern
jobDescription:
About the Role
We are building the next generation of financial automation, and were looking for curious, driven graduates to join us as AI Developer Interns. This is a hands-on learning role where youll work alongside senior engineers and consultants to build real LLM-powered systems - not shadow work or busywork. Youll get exposure to the full lifecycle of an AI product: from understanding a business problem, to building a working prototype, to seeing it used by real clients.

What You Bring
Core (Must-Have)
  • Pursuing or recently completed BE/BTech/MCA, AI/ML, Data Science, or a closely related engineering discipline, with strong academic fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and probability/statistics.
  • Enjoys coding and building things, not just studying theory.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, learning-oriented environment.
  • Eager to research, experiment, and try things hands-on, with support from mentors.
  • Curious about Generative AI, AI Agents, LLMs, Computer Vision, and SaaS platforms.
  • Comfortable "vibe coding" with AI pair-programming tools (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, or similar) to move fast, while still understanding and owning the underlying logic.
  • Genuine interest in AI/LLMs - coursework, personal projects, or self-study count.
  • Strong problem-solving ability and willingness to learn new tools quickly.
  • Good communication skills - comfortable asking questions and explaining your work.
Nice-to-Have

  • Familiarity with FastAPI, Flask, or any Python web framework.

Required Skill Set
Python (FastAPI), LLMs (LangGraph, LangChain, Pydantic), RAG and Vector Databases, AWS and Azure, Vibe coding, PostgreSQL and MongoDB, Docker and Kubernetes, Langfuse/LangSmith for observability.
Why This Role
  • Real work, real impact: Youll contribute to systems used by actual clients, not throwaway assignments.

You will own the roadmap for a critical business area, partner with product and engineering leaders, and guide your team to build and deploy ML models that drive direct business impact.

  • Stakeholder Management Communication: Effectively communicate complex technical concepts and the business impact of your teams work to a diverse audience, including senior leadership.

  • Educational Background: A Bachelor s or Master s in a quantitative field like Computer Science, Statistics, Operations Research, Economics, or a related discipline.
